rv.q: Watching the stage version is like seeing a Technicolor film rendered in black and white: Lez Brotherston's set, with its partitioned steel structures, seems determined to evoke the reality of Cherbourg, whereas the point of the story is that it is a romantic fairytale. The performances themselves are fine.
The approach here is quieter, more low-tech and – if they can do something about that first “mauvais quart d’heure” – just as seductive.
